title: Felix Gonzalez-Torres
edition: Revised and expanded edition (first published 1995 by the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum)

description.main: Nancy Spector's monograph on Felix Gonzalez-Torres, first published for his 1995 Guggenheim retrospective and long the standard text on the artist, reissued by Phaidon in a revised and expanded edition.
description.extended:
Nancy Spector's monograph on Felix Gonzalez-Torres was first published by the Guggenheim Museum for the artist's 1995 retrospective, and it is still the standard text on his work. Phaidon reissues it here in a revised and expanded edition.

Spector reads the work by theme rather than by date. She covers the whole of Gonzalez-Torres's output and sets it against the art of the 1990s. In her account, his conceptual rigor and his personal and political content were one project. Works built to change shape, be taken apart, and be renewed carried meanings about love, loss, public space, and the AIDS crisis. The cloth cover carries a photograph of open water printed as a jigsaw puzzle, a format the artist used for a series of works.

Gonzalez-Torres (1957–1996) was born in Guáimaro, Cuba, and worked in New York. He made candy spills, paper stacks, strings of light bulbs, and billboards that viewers could take from, walk through, or pass on the street. Spector curated the 1995 retrospective as a Guggenheim curator and later served as the museum's Artistic Director and Chief Curator. She is now a Fellow at the Felix Gonzalez-Torres Foundation. The library also holds the Zwirner, Koenig, and Radius books on the artist, and Roni Horn's Steidl volume pairing their work.
description.artist_bio: Felix Gonzalez-Torres (1957–1996) was a Cuban-born American conceptual artist based in New York, known for candy spills, paper stacks, light strings and billboards whose form changes with each installation.
description.exhibition_context: The original edition accompanied the 1995 Gonzalez-Torres retrospective at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York, curated by Nancy Spector.

notes: Revised and expanded edition of Nancy Spector's 1995 Guggenheim Museum monograph. Phaidon lists the book as shipping from 30 November 2026.
